historical_context: Matilda II tanks equipped 4th Armoured Brigade during Operation Battleaxe (June 1941). Heavy armor made them nearly immune to German 37mm and short 50mm guns, but they were too slow for mobile desert operations.

Matilda II Infantry Tank.notes: Heavily armored but slow. Vulnerable to 88mm FlaK guns.

strengths: Immune to most German anti-tank weapons except 88mm
Excellent for frontal assaults against defensive positions
High morale due to heavy protection
weaknesses: Too slow for mobile warfare (24 kph)
QF 2-pounder inadequate against German medium tanks at range
tactical_notes.typical_deployment: Infantry support role. Advance slowly to overrun defensive positions. Best used in coordinated attacks with motorized infantry.
